questions.question: A short story in which animals are given human characteristics and which normally teaches a moral lesson is a ________.
A word whose sound imitates the sound associated with its meaning illustrates ________.
"Jolliba stood in the middle of the road, unafraid of the surging traffic, as if he was no longer alive." The major literary device is ________.
A question asked for effect rather than to obtain an answer is called a ________.

Use the extract below to answer Questions 5–10.

"What say you, Hermia? Be advised, fair maid.
To you your father should be as a god;
One that composed your beauties, yea, and one
To whom you are but as a form in wax,
By him imprinted and within his power
To leave the figure or disfigure it.
Demetrius is a worthy gentleman."

Who is the speaker?
Which of the following is NOT present during the speech in Question 5?
The speaker in Question 5 is addressing ________.
In the line "To you your father should be as a god", Hermia's father is ________.
In the extract, "composed" most nearly means ________.
Where do Lysander and Hermia plan to go in order to escape Athenian law and marry?
In Agostinho Neto's "The Grieved Lands of Africa", the poem is presented as a reflection on the suffering of ________.
Which of the following is a major theme in "The Grieved Lands of Africa"?
Which of the following is a character in John Kolosa Kargbo's "Let Me Die Alone"?
"Let Me Die Alone" contains moments of comic relief.
"The sunshine of her smile left me restless for days." The most prominent literary device in this expression is ________.
Prose is broadly divided into fiction and non-fiction.
An autobiography is ________.
options: A. A story that never existed
C. The story of a person written by another person
D. The story of a person's life written by that person

questions.question: Faction is a type of prose in which ________.
options: A. Fact and fiction are combined

questions.question: The following are techniques used in plot development EXCEPT ________.
A character who does not undergo significant change in the course of a literary work is generally a ________ character.
The physical and social environment in which characters operate is called the ________.
A poem that tells a story is called a ________.
A tercet is a group of three successive ________ in poetry.
options: D. Verses of ten lines each

questions.question: The tragic flaw of a character is also known as ________.
The exchange of ideas between two or more characters in a play is called ________.
Run-on-lines in poetry are also called ________.
A stanza is the poetic equivalent of a paragraph in prose.
Blank verse refers to ________.
options: B. Verse that has not been written
D. Unrhymed verse, usually written in regular metre

questions.question: The general emotional feeling created by a poem is its ________.
"A Midsummer Night's Dream" was written by ________.
Oberon is the king of the ________ in "A Midsummer Night's Dream".
Titania is the ________ in "A Midsummer Night's Dream".
The love potion in "A Midsummer Night's Dream" mainly creates ________.
Hermia is in love with ________.
Helena is in love with ________.
A character who provides humour in an otherwise serious scene performs the function of ________.
A direct comparison in which one thing is said to be another is called a ________.
The repetition of initial consonant sounds in nearby words is known as ________.
A pause within a line of poetry is called a ________.
A fourteen-line poem is generally called a ________.

essay.title: PAPER 2 - THEORY
essay.instruction: Answer four (4) questions. Question One is compulsory.

questions.question: Discuss the background and setting of Agostinho Neto's poem "The Grieved Lands of Africa". (10 marks)

Discuss the following themes in William Shakespeare's "A Midsummer Night's Dream":
(a) Magic
(b) The difficulties of love. (10 marks)
Discuss Oberon's love potion as a representation of power and the instability of love in "A Midsummer Night's Dream". (10 marks)

(a) List two characters in "A Midsummer Night's Dream". (2 marks)
(b) List and explain four literary devices used in "Let Me Die Alone". (8 marks)

(a) List two characters in "Let Me Die Alone". (2 marks)
(b) Discuss the physical setting and imagery in Maya Angelou's "Caged Bird". (8 marks)
